title: Recursive settings merger drops falsy overrides

crosscheck.reference: recursive two-pass merge (copy defaults, then apply overrides; dict+dict recurse)

cases.name: v4:inputs_untouched
cases.code: d={'a': {'b': 1}}; o={'a': {'c': 2}}; r=sol.merge_settings(d,o); result=(d, o, r)

cases.name: v4:returns_new_dict_not_an_input
cases.code:
d = {'a': 1}; o = {'b': 2}
r = sol.merge_settings(d, o)
r['zz'] = 9
result = (r is d, r is o, d, o, sorted(r))

cases.name: all_falsy_overrides
cases.code:
import copy
out = []
for d, o in [({'a': True, 'b': 1, 'c': 'x', 'd': [1], 'e': {'k': 1}, 'f': 2.5}, {'a': False, 'b': 0, 'c': '', 'd': [], 'f': 0.0, 'e': None})]:
    dc, oc = copy.deepcopy(d), copy.deepcopy(o)
    r = sol.merge_settings(d, o)
    out.append((r, type(r).__name__, r is not d and r is not o, d == dc, o == oc))
result = out
